fact: Typhoon Nina dropped a year's worth of rain in approximately six hours over the Banqiao Dam area
source: Human Impacts on Weather and Climate, William R. Cotton & Roger A. Pielke Sr. (2007); also widely documented in hydrology literature. The storm dropped approximately 1,060 mm in 24 hours, with the heaviest rainfall concentrated in a roughly 6-hour period, against an annual average of about 800 mm.

fact: The dam's sluice gates were clogged with sediment, preventing proper water release
source: The River Dragon Has Come! The Three Gorges Dam and the Fate of China's Yangtze River and Its People, Dai Qing (1998). Sedimentation blocking sluice gates is a widely cited factor in the dam's failure.

fact: Sixty-one dams failed in the cascade triggered by Typhoon Nina
source: Widely documented figure: 62 dams failed in total (Banqiao and Shimantan plus 60 others). Cited in Discovery Channel documentary and multiple engineering analyses.

fact: Approximately 200,000 people died as a result of the Banqiao Dam collapse and subsequent flooding
source: Human Rights Watch / Probe International estimates cite 171,000–240,000 deaths (including famine and epidemics in the aftermath). The figure of ~230,000 total deaths is from Dai Qing's 'The River Dragon Has Come!' and Chinese government reassessments.

fact: Authorities denied requests to open floodgates to protect the downstream harvest
source: The River Dragon Has Come! The Three Gorges Dam and the Fate of China's Yangtze River and Its People, Dai Qing (1998). Communication failures and bureaucratic reluctance to authorize releases are documented, though the exact 'harvest' rationale is a simplified but commonly cited explanation.
